questions.q: A canteen manager noted the samosas sold on five days: 120, 135, 128, 140 and 132. Which question can this record help to answer?
questions.a: How many samosas does the canteen usually sell in a day?
o: How many samosas does the canteen usually sell in a day?
How many samosas were sold on the day with the 140 sale?
Did the canteen sell any samosas on Monday?
How many samosas fit on one plate at the canteen?

questions.q: True or False: A question is a statistical question whenever its answer is a number. Give the verdict and a reason or correction.
questions.a: False. 'How many days are there in September?' has a number as its answer, but it has one fixed answer and needs no data collected. A statistical question is one answered by collecting data that is expected to vary.
s: Reason or correction: a numerical answer can still be fixed; a statistical question needs varying data

questions.q: Dev claims, 'Any question that uses the word average is a statistical question.' Which question shows that Dev is wrong?
questions.a: What is the average of the numbers 12 and 18?
o: What is the average of the numbers 12 and 18?
What is the average number of brothers and sisters of Class 7 students?
What is the average time Class 7 students take to eat lunch?
What is the average pocket money of children in our colony?

questions.q: Which pair correctly shows a question with one fixed answer and a statistical question made from it?
questions.a: 'How long did Ananya's bus ride take today?' becomes 'How long do Class 7 students' bus rides usually take?'
o: 'How long did Ananya's bus ride take today?' becomes 'How long do Class 7 students' bus rides usually take?'
'How tall is Ananya?' becomes 'How tall is Ananya, in millimetres?'
'What was the noon temperature today?' becomes 'What was the noon temperature today, in kelvin?'
'How many pages does this notebook have?' becomes 'How many pages does this notebook have, counted twice?'

questions.q: At the school fair Kabir asked five Class 7 students how much they spent at the food stalls: Rs 20, Rs 35, Rs 20, Rs 50 and Rs 25. Which statistical statement do these figures support?
questions.a: The five students Kabir asked spent about Rs 30 each on average.
o: The five students Kabir asked spent about Rs 30 each on average.
Every Class 7 student spends Rs 30 at the food stalls.
The food stalls earned Rs 150 in all on the fair day.
Kabir spent Rs 20, so students usually spend Rs 20.

questions.q: A cricketer scored 41, 45, 38, 44 and 42 in her last five matches. One coach says, 'She will score exactly 42 tomorrow.' Another says, 'She will probably score between 38 and 45.' Which is the statistical way to speak, and why?
questions.a: The second, because a statistical statement says what is likely from past data, not what is certain
o: The second, because a statistical statement says what is likely from past data, not what is certain
The first, because the mean of her five scores is 42, so tomorrow's score is fixed
The second, because a prediction from data can never turn out wrong
Neither, because five matches give no information about tomorrow

questions.q: Ravi guesses that the taller of two friends, 6 ft against 5 ft, is a man. They turn out to be a 6-foot woman and a 5-foot man. What should Ravi conclude?
questions.a: The guess failed this time, but guessing from height is still reasonable because it is right more often than not
o: The guess failed this time, but guessing from height is still reasonable because it is right more often than not
The guess proves that no man is ever 5 ft tall
Guessing from height is useless because it failed once
The guess should have been right, so the friends' heights must have been recorded wrongly

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 'How long does a Class 7 student take to solve a sudoku?' is a statistical question.

questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Statement 1: 'What fraction of Class 7 students walk to school?' is a statistical question, since its answer comes from collecting data that varies from child to child.
Statement 2: A prediction made from past data is a statistical statement only when it is certain to come true.
Statement 3: 'How many students are on the Class 7A roll today?' has one fixed answer found by counting, so it is not a statistical question.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only
o: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Match each item in Column I with the description in Column II that fits it best.
Column I: 1. A survey of the number of siblings of every Class 7 student  2. 'Typically, is milk costlier in Pune or in Nagpur?'  3. 'My phone battery lasts about 9 hours on average.'  4. 'On which date is Diwali this year?'
Column II: a. a statistical statement that summarises data with an average  b. a question with one fixed answer, no data needed  c. a statistical question answered by comparing prices over time  d. a statistical question about a group whose answers vary

Sana timed three Class 7 students reading the same story: 12, 15 and 18 minutes. (a) Find the mean time. (b) She writes, 'So every Class 7 student takes 15 minutes.' Rewrite her sentence as a correct statistical statement.
questions.a: (a) (12 + 15 + 18) / 3 = 45 / 3 = 15 minutes. (b) For example: The three students I timed took 15 minutes on average, so Class 7 students probably take about 15 minutes, though three students are a small sample.
s: Part (b): a statement about the timed group or a likely value, not 'every student'

questions.q: (a) Which of these two questions needs data to be collected, and why: 'How many legs does a spider have?' or 'How many pets does a Class 7 student have?' (b) Give one statistical question about spiders.
questions.a: (a) The pets question: the answer differs from child to child, so data from many children is needed. Every spider has the same number of legs, so that answer is fixed. (b) For example: How long are the spiders found in our school garden?
s: Part (a): picks the pets question because its answers vary, and says the spider answer is fixed
Part (b): a question about spiders whose answers are expected to vary

questions.q: A bowler took 2, 3, 1, 4 and 0 wickets in five matches. (a) Write one statistical statement using these numbers. (b) Write a statistical question that these numbers help to answer.
questions.a: (a) She took 10 wickets in 5 matches, that is 2 wickets per match on average. (b) How many wickets does she usually take in a match?
s: Part (a): a statement with a number from the data (total 10 or average 2)
Part (b): a question that expects varied answers and needs this data

questions.q: (a) Say whether each is a statistical question, a statistical statement, or a question that is not statistical: (i) 'Most Class 7 students prefer cricket.' (ii) 'Which game do Class 7 students prefer?' (iii) 'Is cricket played with a bat?' (b) Rewrite (ii) as a statistical statement using 18 out of 30 students.
questions.a: (a) (i) statistical statement; (ii) statistical question; (iii) a question that is not statistical, since it has one fixed answer. (b) 18 out of 30 Class 7 students, that is 3 out of 5, prefer cricket.
s: Part (b): a statement with 18 out of 30 (3 out of 5)

questions.q: Ritu measured the heights of 20 classmates, then wrote them in order from smallest to largest. This year's mean is 146 cm and last year's class mean was 143 cm. (a) Which activity of statistics is writing the heights in order? (b) She says, 'This class is 3 cm taller on average.' Which activity is this, and is the 3 cm correct?
questions.a: (a) Organising the data. (b) Interpreting the data; yes, 146 - 143 = 3 cm is correct.
s: Part (b): interpreting, and the difference 3 cm checked

questions.q: Rafi says, 'Kavya timed one Class 7 student cycling home in 15 minutes. Since different students take different times, "How long do Class 7 students take to cycle home?" is still a statistical question.' Do you agree? Give two reasons.
questions.a: Yes. The question asks about a whole group, and the times are expected to vary from child to child. It can only be answered by collecting many times, whereas Kavya's single reading is one value, not the answer.
s: Gives the verdict that Rafi is right
Reason: the answers are expected to vary across students
Reason: it needs data from many students, not one reading

questions.q: A survey sheet has three questions: (i) 'How many brothers and sisters do Class 7 students have?' (ii) 'How many days are there in February of a leap year?' (iii) 'How much did Nikhil spend on lunch today?' Which one is already a statistical question? For each of the others, say why it is not and rewrite it into a statistical question on the same topic.
questions.a: (i) is statistical: the answers differ from child to child. (ii) has one fixed answer, 29; a statistical version is: How many rainy days does our town usually have in February? (iii) is about one person on one day; a statistical version is: How much do Class 7 students usually spend on lunch?
s: Picks (i) with the reason that the answers vary
(ii) is fixed, with a valid statistical rewrite
(iii) is one person on one day, with a valid statistical rewrite

questions.q: Choose the topic 'pocket money in your class'. Write (i) one statistical question and (ii) one statistical statement with a number. (iii) Say how the statement could be checked.
questions.a: (i) How much pocket money does a Class 7 student get each week? (ii) Most students in our class get about ₹50 a week. (iii) Collect each student's weekly amount and compare with the statement by finding the typical value.
s: A valid statistical question on the topic
A statement that uses a numerical value
Says the statement is checked by collecting the data

questions.q: At the Class 7 sports day, Ms Verma wants to know how long her students take to run 100 m. Five students took 16, 18, 15, 17 and 16 seconds. (a) Write a statistical question for her. (b) Find the total and the average time. (c) Write a statistical statement. (d) Why must she collect more than one student's time?
questions.a: (a) How long do Class 7 students take to run 100 m? (b) total 16+18+15+17+16 = 82 s, average 82/5 = 16.4 s. (c) The students took about 16.4 seconds on average. (d) One time is one answer; times vary, so many values are needed to describe the group.
s: Part (c): a statement using the numbers
Part (d): says answers vary so many values are needed

questions.q: Mrs Rao, the school librarian, noted the books issued on six school days: Monday 12, Tuesday 18, Wednesday 9, Thursday 15, Friday 21, Saturday 15. Her rule is to restock when more than 100 books are issued in a week. (a) Is 'How many books does the library issue on a typical day?' a statistical question? Why? (b) How many books were issued in the six days? (c) Write one statistical statement using the average per day. (d) Should she restock now, or keep recording for more weeks? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Yes: the daily numbers vary from day to day and need data. (b) 12 + 18 + 9 + 15 + 21 + 15 = 90 books. (c) On average 15 books were issued per day (90 / 6). (d) She should not restock yet. By her rule 90 is below 100; the days range from 9 to 21, and one week is too small a sample to say a typical week is near 100, so she should keep recording for more weeks and restock only if the weekly total passes 100.
s: Part (a): yes because daily numbers vary and need data
Part (c): statement with average 15 per day
Part (d): decision not to restock yet, justified by 90 < 100 and the small sample of one week

questions.q: Four students make claims. Neha: 'On average our class is taller than yours.' Imran: 'The school bell rang at 8 a.m. today.' Joseph: 'Most Class 7 students cycle to school.' Sakshi: 'What is the date of the school fair?' (a) Which two claims are statistical statements? (b) Which one is a question, and is it a statistical question? (c) Rewrite Neha's claim as a statistical statement that uses two numbers. (d) Give a statistical question that Joseph's claim could answer.
questions.a: (a) Neha's (it summarises and compares groups) and Joseph's (a proportion, most). Imran's is a single fact for one moment, not a summary of data. (b) Sakshi's; not statistical, it has one fixed answer. (c) For example: The mean height of our class is 146 cm and of yours is 143 cm. (d) How do Class 7 students come to school?
s: Part (a): picks Neha and Joseph with a reason
Part (b): picks Sakshi and says it is not statistical
Part (c): a statement with two numbers comparing the classes
Part (d): a statistical question on travel to school

questions.q: Sneha tells her mother, 'I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home.' To check, she timed herself on five days and got 14, 18, 15, 22 and 16 minutes. Her mother wants to start the pressure cooker just before she arrives. (a) Write a statistical question that Sneha's timings help to answer. (b) Find the total time and the mean time. (c) Does the data support 'about 15 minutes'? (d) What should Sneha tell her mother about her arrival time, so that the lunch is neither cold nor wasted?
questions.a: (a) How long does Sneha usually take to cycle home? (b) total 85 minutes, mean 17 minutes. (c) Not really: the mean is 17; three of the five days were 16 minutes or more, and one was 22. (d) Say she usually takes about 17 minutes and may take up to about 22; start the cooker after she leaves school.
s: Part (a): a statistical question about her usual time
Part (c): compares 15 with 17 and the spread
Part (d): a justified recommendation using mean and the range

questions.q: Five children collect 4, 9, 11, 6 and 5 guavas. The child who collected 11 leaves with them, and the other four share the rest equally. Each of the four gets ___ guavas.
Class 7A (8 students) collects 48 notebooks and Class 7B (6 students) collects 42 notebooks for a drive. Each class shares its notebooks equally among its own students. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: Each 7B student gets 1 notebook more than each 7A student
o: Each 7B student gets 1 notebook more than each 7A student
Each 7A student gets more because 7A has the bigger total
Each student gets the same number in both classes
Each 7B student gets 6 notebooks more than each 7A student

questions.q: Five buckets hold 4, 9, 2, 7 and 3 litres of water. Water may be poured from bucket to bucket, with none thrown away, until all five hold the same amount. How much does each bucket then hold?
questions.a: 5 litres
o: 5 litres
9 litres
2 litres
4 litres

questions.q:
Match each situation in Column I with its mean in Column II.
Column I: 1. Daily steps (thousands) in 4 days: 4, 6, 8, 6  2. Flowers on a plant over 5 days: 2, 0, 7, 3, 3  3. Three friends hold 9, 15 and 12 marbles and share equally  4. Runs in 4 matches: 0, 30, 21, 9
Column II: a. 3   b. 6   c. 12   d. 15
Five friends collect 6, 9, 4, 7 and 4 mangoes. A sixth friend, who has collected none, joins and they all share equally. How many mangoes does each of the six get?

At the Republic Day camp, Team A of 5 scouts collects 40 bottles of used plastic and Team B of 8 scouts collects 56 bottles. Both teams share bottles equally within the team. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: A gets 8 each and B gets 7 each, so A members get more per scout
o: A gets 8 each and B gets 7 each, so A members get more per scout
Team B members get more because the team total 56 is bigger than 40
Both teams get equal shares because both collected a whole number of bottles

questions.q:
Statement 1: The average of a group can be understood as a fair share.
Statement 2: If two groups have different numbers of members, a bigger total always means a bigger average.
Statement 3: The mean of 5, 7 and 9 is 8.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q: After 4 matches a batter's average is 20 runs. In the fifth match she scores 50. What is her new average?

Assertion (A): Club P scored 84 runs in 4 matches and Club Q scored 100 runs in 5 matches, so Club P has the higher average.
Reason (R): Mean = total runs divided by the number of matches played.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: The mean number of flowers on a hibiscus plant over 6 days was 5. When the seventh day was added, the mean of the 7 days became 6. (a) Find the total for the first 6 days. (b) How many flowers bloomed on the seventh day?
questions.a: (a) 5 x 6 = 30 flowers. (b) The new total is 6 x 7 = 42, so the seventh day had 42 - 30 = 12 flowers.

questions.q: A group of 6 children has a mean of 8 marbles each. (a) How many marbles do they hold altogether? (b) Two more children join, holding 15 and 5 marbles. Find the new mean and say by how much it has gone up or down.
questions.a: (a) 6 x 8 = 48 marbles. (b) The total becomes 48 + 15 + 5 = 68 for 8 children, so the mean is 68 / 8 = 8.5, up by 0.5.

questions.q: Asha's mean in her first 4 unit tests (each out of 30) is 18. (a) What mark in the fifth test makes her mean for 5 tests exactly 20? (b) If she scores that mark, what must she score in a sixth test for the mean of 6 tests to be 21?
questions.a: (a) Total needed 20 x 5 = 100, and her first four total 18 x 4 = 72, so she needs 28. (b) Total needed 21 x 6 = 126, so the sixth mark is 126 - 72 - 28 = 26.

questions.q: Dhruv says, 'Club A scored 215 runs in 5 matches and Club B scored 192 runs in 4 matches. A has the bigger total so A batted better.' Do you agree? Support your answer with numbers.
questions.a: No. The groups are different sizes, so totals mislead. Club A's mean is 215 / 5 = 43 runs a match and Club B's is 192 / 4 = 48, so B did better per match.
s: Verdict that Dhruv is wrong because the number of matches differs

questions.q: Anil's five 100 m trial times were 16, 17, 15, 18 and 16 seconds. Bela's four trial times were 17, 15, 16 and 15 seconds (she missed the fifth). (a) Find each runner's mean time. (b) Who is quicker on average and by how much? Why does the gap between their totals overstate the difference?
questions.a: (a) Anil: 82 / 5 = 16.4 s. Bela: 63 / 4 = 15.75 s. (b) Bela is quicker by 16.4 - 15.75 = 0.65 s on average. The totals differ by 19 s only because Bela has one run fewer, so the totals are not comparable.
s: Part (b): Bela quicker by 0.65 s, and the totals differ because the number of runs differs

questions.q: Show that the mean of 12, 15, 18 and 21 cannot be 25 or 10.
questions.a: The mean levels the values out, so it lies between the smallest and the largest value: 12 and 21. The actual mean is 66 / 4 = 16.5. 25 is above 21 and 10 is below 12, so neither is possible.
s: States that the mean lies between smallest and largest

questions.q: Five children hold 7, 3, 9, 5 and 11 marbles. They pass marbles among themselves until each has the same number. (a) How many marbles does each child end with? (b) How many marbles must the child holding 11 give away, and how many must the child holding 3 receive?
questions.a: (a) Total 35, so each ends with 35 / 5 = 7 marbles, the mean. (b) The child with 11 gives away 11 - 7 = 4 marbles; the child with 3 receives 7 - 3 = 4 marbles.

questions.q: The mean marks of a student in 5 tests is 72. (a) Find the total of her 5 marks. (b) Four of the marks are 68, 75, 80 and 65. Find the fifth. (c) What mark in a sixth test (out of 100) makes her mean for 6 tests 75? (d) Can she reach a mean of 80 over 6 tests? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 72 x 5 = 360. (b) 360 - (68 + 75 + 80 + 65) = 360 - 288 = 72. (c) 75 x 6 = 450, so 450 - 360 = 90. (d) A mean of 80 needs a total of 480, so the sixth mark would be 120, more than 100. Not possible.
s: Part (c): sixth mark 90 with the method total = mean x number
Part (d): needs 120 which exceeds 100, so impossible

questions.q: A railway booking counter sold 3150, 3480, 3610, 3200, 3920 and 3640 tickets in six consecutive weeks. (a) Find the mean number of tickets per week. (b) In how many of the six weeks were the sales above the mean?
questions.a: (a) Total 21000, mean 21000 / 6 = 3500. (b) 3610, 3920 and 3640 are above 3500, so 3 weeks.

questions.q: A farmer in Wayanad records rainfall in mm on five days: 12, 0, 25, 8 and 15. A day with no rain is recorded as 0. He irrigates his pepper plants when the rainfall so far looks below 14 mm a day. (a) Find the mean rainfall for the five days. (b) Should the zero be counted as a day? Explain. (c) On day six the gauge shows 30 mm. Find the new mean and the new median. (d) His neighbour says the two heavy showers (25 mm and 30 mm) run off the soil, so the median is a truer guide than the mean. Which measure would you advise him to use for deciding to irrigate on day six, and why?
questions.a: (a) 60 / 5 = 12 mm. (b) Yes: a 0 means the day was measured and no rain fell, so the day counts. (c) Mean (60 + 30) / 6 = 15 mm; the sorted values 0, 8, 12, 15, 25, 30 give a median of (12 + 15) / 2 = 13.5 mm. (d) The mean 15 says do not irrigate and the median 13.5 says irrigate. Since the two big showers pull the mean up and three of the six days had 12 mm or less, the median is the better guide and he should irrigate; an answer for the mean must say the plants did receive the 25 and 30 mm.
s: Part (b): counts the zero with a reason
Part (d): chooses a measure and justifies it using the outlier showers and the two values

questions.q: Two groups of children share paper cranes equally within the group. Group P (4 children) folded 9, 12, 7 and 8 cranes. Group Q (6 children) folded 6, 8, 5, 9, 7 and 5 cranes. (a) Find the total of each group. (b) Find each child's equal share in each group. (c) Which group has the greater total and which the greater share? (d) Which measure should be used to say which group did better, and why?
questions.a: (a) P: 36, Q: 40. (b) P: 36 / 4 = 9, Q: 40 / 6 = 6.67 (about 6.7). (c) Q has the greater total, P the greater share. (d) The mean, because the groups differ in size and the mean is the fair share per child.
s: Part (d): chooses the mean with a reason about unequal group sizes

questions.q: Classes 7A and 7B ran a savings drive for a flood-relief fund. The six students of the 7A savings club saved ₹240, 180, 300, 120, 260 and 100. The eight students of the 7B club saved ₹150, 200, 170, 220, 90, 280, 160 and 250. The principal can give a trophy for either the larger collection or the larger saving per student. (a) Find the total saved by each club. (b) Find each club's mean saving per student. (c) What does the mean tell us here in terms of equal shares? (d) The principal must pick one measure for the trophy. Which would you advise, and what is the case for the other measure?
questions.a: (a) 7A: 1200, 7B: 1520. (b) 7A: 200, 7B: 190. (c) If every student had saved the same amount, each of 7A would have saved 200 and each of 7B 190. (d) Per-student mean favours 7A and is fair when clubs differ in size; the total favours 7B because it has more members. Either is defensible but the mean is fairer to a smaller club.
s: Part (c): explains the mean as an equal share
Part (d): a justified choice that weighs both measures

questions.q: Tomato prices in a town ranged from Rs 21 to Rs 58 in one month. In the next month the lowest price fell by Rs 2 and the highest rose by Rs 9, so the range became ___ rupees.
Weekly rainfall (cm) in two villages over five weeks was: Village A 12, 14, 13, 15, 12 and Village B 2, 30, 5, 25, 3. Which statement is justified by these figures?
questions.a: Village A's rain was steadier: its range is 3, Village B's is 28
o: Village A's rain was steadier: its range is 3, Village B's is 28
Village B had more rain in all weeks because it reached the highest value, 30
Village B varied less because its total, 65, is smaller than 66
The two villages vary equally because both have five readings

questions.q: Zara has a dot plot and a column graph of the same 12 monthly prices of a town. She wants to know in which month the price first crossed Rs 40. Which can answer this, and why?
questions.a: Only the column graph, because it keeps the months in order and the dot plot does not
o: Only the column graph, because it keeps the months in order and the dot plot does not
Only the dot plot, because the dots are sorted and the first dot above 40 is the first month
Both, because each dot is labelled with its month
Neither, because a graph cannot show when a price changed

questions.q: A dot plot of a shop's customers over 10 days has these stacks: 20 (two dots), 22 (one dot), 25 (three dots), 28 (one dot), 30 (two dots) and 35 (one dot). On how many days did the shop have more than 25 customers?
questions.a: 4 days
o: 4 days
3 days
7 days
10 days

questions.q: Over 8 months, milk prices in Town P ranged from Rs 30 to Rs 75, and in Town Q from Rs 45 to Rs 80. Which conclusion is justified by these figures?
questions.a: Town P's prices varied more: its range is 45, against 35 for Town Q
o: Town P's prices varied more: its range is 45, against 35 for Town Q
Town Q's prices varied more because its highest price, Rs 80, is larger
The two towns varied equally because both ranges start above Rs 25
Town P was costlier throughout because its range is larger

questions.q:
Statement 1: For the data 12, 7, 19 and 14, the range is 12.
Statement 2: Two data sets with the same total can have very different ranges.
Statement 3: If the range of a data set is 0, every value in it is the same.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1, 2 and 3
o: 1, 2 and 3
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only

questions.q: A dot plot of daily steps (in thousands) over 12 days has 9 dots between 6 and 8, and three single dots at 2, 3 and 14. Ruchi says, 'The range is 8 - 6 = 2.' What is her mistake, and what is the correct range?
questions.a: She used the cluster instead of the lowest and highest values; the range is 14 - 2 = 12 thousand steps
o: She used the cluster instead of the lowest and highest values; the range is 14 - 2 = 12 thousand steps
She should have added the ends; the range is 14 + 2 = 16 thousand steps
She is right, because the range is the width of the biggest cluster
She used the lowest cluster value; the range is 14 - 6 = 8 thousand steps

questions.q:
For the data 12, 7, 19, 14, match each measure in Column I with its value in Column II.
Column I: 1. Range  2. Total  3. Mean  4. Minimum
Column II: a. 7   b. 13   c. 12   d. 52

Assertion (A): Two towns can have the same mean milk price, yet one town's prices can vary far more than the other's.
Reason (R): The range uses only the highest and the lowest values, whereas the mean uses every value.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: The heights (cm) of seven plants are 24, 31, 28, 35, 27, 31 and 30. (a) Find the minimum, maximum and range. (b) How many plants are taller than the minimum by more than 5 cm?
questions.a: (a) Minimum 24, maximum 35, range 11. (b) Heights above 29: 31, 35, 31, 30 are 4 plants.

questions.q: A dot plot of 8 weekly tomato prices (Rs per kg) has dots at 20, 22, 22, 25, 25, 25, 30 and 48. (a) Find the range and say where the cluster lies. (b) Which value lies far from the cluster, and what does the range become if that value is left out?
questions.a: (a) Range 48 - 20 = 28; seven of the eight prices cluster between 20 and 30 (mostly 20 to 25). (b) The price 48 lies far from the cluster; without it the range is 30 - 20 = 10.
s: Part (a): range 28 and the cluster at about 20 to 30
Part (b): picks 48 and gives the new range 10

questions.q: Team A scored 14, 9, 11, 16, 10 and 12 points in six games and Team B scored 13, 13, 12, 14 and 13 points in five games. (a) Find each team's total. (b) Explain why the totals alone cannot say which team scored better per game.
questions.a: (a) A: 72, B: 65. (b) A played 6 games and B played 5, so the totals count different numbers of games; the means 12 and 13 should be compared.
s: Part (b): says the numbers of games differ so means are needed

questions.q: A canteen sold 40, 52, 46, 40 and 62 samosas on five days. (a) Find the total and the range. (b) On five other days the canteen also sold 240 samosas in total, but the range was only 6. Which week is steadier, and which measure tells you?
questions.a: (a) Total 240; range 62 - 40 = 22. (b) The second set of five days is steadier, because its range (6) is smaller; the totals are equal so the total cannot tell them apart.
s: Part (b): second week, using the range since totals are equal

questions.q: A shopkeeper's daily sales (₹ thousand) in Pune for six days are 18, 22, 15, 30, 25 and 20. (a) Find the total sales. (b) Find the range. (c) If days are grouped as 15-20, 21-25 and 26-30, which group holds the most days?

questions.a: (a) Boys 3.6, 4, 3.2 units; girls 4.4, 3, 4 units. (b) Sections A and C.

questions.q: A report says: 'On a graph with 1 unit = 20 rockets, a company's bars for 2021, 2022 and 2023 are 3, 6 and 7.5 units long, and the company launched 300 rockets in the three years.' Show that the report contradicts itself.

questions.q: Reema practised a 400 m lap and noted her times in seconds. Week 1: 95, 92, 98, 90, 94, 96, 93. Week 2: 90, 88, 92, 86, 89, 91, 87. Her coach says, 'You have improved, so you will run under 85 seconds in the next race.' (a) Find the mean time of each week. (b) By how much did the mean fall? (c) Find the range of each week. (d) Is the coach's prediction justified by the data? Give a reason for and one against.
questions.a: (a) Week 1: 658 / 7 = 94; Week 2: 623 / 7 = 89. (b) 5 seconds. (c) 8 and 6. (d) For: times fell by 5 s a week and the best Week 2 time is 86. Against: the trend may not continue, and the fastest time was 86, so under 85 is not certain. It is a possible but not a justified certainty.
s: Part (d): a balanced judgement on the prediction
